evidence_items.source_text: A chest radiograph (Figure 1a) showed blunting of both costophrenic angles as well as bibasilar infiltrates and atelectasis, predominant in the right lower lung field, and associated with bilateral volume loss. A hemodialysis catheter in adequate position and an electronic device overlying the heart were seen. A rounded opaque structure is noted at the level of the main right bronchus.
This opaque structure was present on chest radiographs performed one month (not shown) and two months earlier (Figure 1b).
Chest computed tomography (CT) (Figure 2) showed a round dense structure located within the right main bronchus, probably aspirated by the patient.
A bronchospy was performed and a metal dental crown was removed.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: A metal dental crown was removed [from the right main bronchus].
